title: Collapse of the USSR
examples: What were the main reasons the Soviet Union fell apart?
How did Gorbachev's policies affect the USSR?
Can you explain the events of 1989 to 1991?

explain.say: The Soviet Union faced many problems by the late 1980s.
Mikhail Gorbachev introduced changes to revitalize the country.
Glasnost meant greater openness in public discussion and media.
Perestroika involved restructuring the failing Soviet economy.
The period from 1989 to 1991 saw many republics declaring independence.
In everyday life, the desire for self-determination is common.

faq.a: He introduced reforms because the Soviet Union's economy and political system were struggling badly. He wanted to save the country from collapse.
asks: What was the goal of Gorbachev's changes?
Why did the USSR need reform?

faq.q: What is the difference between Glasnost and Perestroika?
faq.a: Glasnost meant political openness and freedom of speech. Perestroika focused on restructuring the economic system for improvement.
asks: Are they related to the economy or politics?

faq.q: Why did the republics want to leave the USSR?
faq.a: The republics felt they had more control over their own lives and resources. They wanted to establish their own independent nations.
asks: What caused the desire for independence?
Why did national groups push for separation?

faq.q: Was the collapse sudden or gradual?
faq.a: It was a gradual process accelerated by political and economic failures. The tensions built up over several years.
asks: Did it happen all at once?
What was the timeline of the collapse?

faq.q: What was the role of the Berlin Wall?
faq.a: The fall of the Berlin Wall symbolized the end of Soviet control over Eastern Europe. It showed that communism's grip was weakening.
asks: Why is the Wall important to this topic?
What did the Wall's fall mean?

facts: Glasnost promoted greater freedom of speech and transparency.
Perestroika aimed to restructure the Soviet economy.
The USSR officially dissolved in December 1991.
The Baltic states were among the first to declare independence.

quiz.say: The policy of openness and discussion was called:
quiz.why: Glasnost directly relates to increased transparency and freedom of speech.

wrong.1: This term refers only to economic restructuring, not openness.
wrong.2: This is the final event, not a policy name.
wrong.3: This is the overall ideology, not the specific reform policy.

quiz.say: Restructuring the Soviet economy was the goal of:
quiz.why: Perestroika specifically targeted making changes to the economic structure.

wrong.0: Independence is the result, not the reform policy itself.
wrong.1: This was a major event, but not the name of the economic plan.
wrong.3: Glasnost deals with political openness, not economic rebuilding.

quiz.say: If a republic wanted to leave the Union, they were expressing a desire for:
quiz.why: Self-determination is the right of a people to choose their own political status.

wrong.0: Openness is a political tool, not the goal of separation.
wrong.1: Dissolution is the act of ending, while self-determination is the underlying right.
wrong.3: Restructuring is an internal change, not a desire for separation.
